The request

Subject: Does Cedar Loop's pickup delay rate warrant immediate permanent staffing or a bounded audit pilot?
RO
VP of Retail Operations
To: Lead Operations Analyst (you)

Hi Lead Operations Analyst,

Whether to authorize permanent evening fulfillment staff based on audit sample delays or mandate a bounded verification pilot before spending capital.

Specifically, I need answers to 4 questions:

  1. 1. Sampling Frame and Nonresponse Audit
    Part A
  2. 2. Duration Estimation and Confidence Intervals
    Part B
  3. 3. Proportion Confidence Interval and Sample Size Planning
    Part C
  4. 4. Post-Class Reflection and Decision Revisit
    Take-home

For this practice:

  • Keep your completed workbook for discussion and your own review.
  • This is ungraded practice. No memo, upload, submission or deadline is required.

Thank you.

Best,
VP of Retail Operations
Cedar Loop Grocery Pickup

Before class: get ready (untimed)

  1. Unzip S05P_Student_Package.zip into one folder.
    Keep every file together. SPSS looks for the CSV files next to the syntax.
  2. Open S05P_Learning_Workbook.xlsx and go to the Start Here sheet.
    Type your first name, last name and NetID (the part before @nyu.edu). Use File › Save As with the workbook name it shows.
  3. Open S05P_SPSS.sps in SPSS and update the CD command.
    Replace REPLACE_WITH_FOLDER_CONTAINING_CSV_AND_SPS with the path of your unzipped lab folder (the folder, not the .sps file; see Find your folder path). Save As the .sps name shown on Start Here.
  4. Select the whole H0 block, then choose Run › Selection.
    The Output Viewer opens with H0 Import and Frame Check.
✅ Ready when: the H0 output shows the expected case count and your workbook is saved under your own name.
⚠️ Stuck? Don't start Part A on the timer. Ask for help first, or see the SPSS environment guide.

Find your folder path (for the CD line)

SPSS needs the path of the folder you unzipped, the one that holds S05P_SPSS.sps and the CSV files. It is not the path to the .sps file. If you open the folder and see the .sps file and the CSV files inside, that is the right folder.

Windows
  1. Unzip first: right-click S05P_Student_Package.zip › Extract All › Extract. Do not work inside the zip.
  2. Open the extracted S05P_Student_Package folder, then the Student folder inside it. You should now see S05P_SPSS.sps and the CSV files. This is your lab folder.
  3. Click once in the address bar at the top of File Explorer: it turns into the path. Press Ctrl+C.
  4. Or: go up one level, hold Shift, right-click that folder › Copy as path, then delete the double quotes it adds.

Looks like C:\Users\you\Downloads\S05P_Student_Package\Student

Mac
  1. Unzip first: double-click S05P_Student_Package.zip in Finder.
  2. Open the extracted S05P_Student_Package folder, then the Student folder inside it. You should now see S05P_SPSS.sps and the CSV files. This is your lab folder.
  3. Go up one level and click that folder once to select it (the folder, not a file inside it). Press Option+Command+C (Copy as Pathname), or right-click it, hold Option and choose Copy … as Pathname.

Looks like /Users/you/Downloads/S05P_Student_Package/Student

Paste it between the single quotes on the CD line:

CD 'C:\Users\you\Downloads\S05P_Student_Package\Student'.      * Windows
CD '/Users/you/Downloads/S05P_Student_Package/Student'.          * Mac
⚠️ Common mistakes: the path ends in /S05P_SPSS.sps (remove the file name); the quotes or the final period are missing; the files are still inside the zip; OneDrive or iCloud has not finished downloading the folder. If H0 says a file cannot be found, check the path first. If the path itself contains an apostrophe ('), put the path in double quotes instead, for example CD "/Users/you/Kim's files/S05P_Student_Package/Student".

Yellow cells: you type hereLavender cells: guidance✓ Check your work: in-class boxes turn to “✓ Checked”; take-home boxes read “Entry recorded” once each answer is a formula

sheet IN-CLASS_Lab Part A · answers email question 1

Part A · Sampling Frame and Nonresponse Audit

⏱ 10 min
From slide 28 → work this card → Back to slide 29 · bring: The nonresponse sensitivity range [19.2%, 39.2%] and its relation to the 20% target.

What the session covered · Section 1 Sampling Design, Bias, and the Limits of Generalization

  • Target Population and Sampling Frame: A target population is the complete group of decision interest, while the sampling frame is the concrete operational list used to draw units. Assuming an internal transactional database automatically includes all customers without duplicate or canceled orders.
  • Nonresponse Sensitivity Bounds: Nonresponse sensitivity bounds establish extreme best-case and worst-case scenario intervals for unobserved units in an audited sample. Treating the 24.0% respondent rate as the true rate while ignoring the 25 missing outcomes.

Target Population and Sampling Frame

N=Total audited frame units N = \text{Total audited frame units}

Nonresponse Sensitivity Bounds

pmin=xrespnselected,pmax=xresp+mnselected p_{\text{min}} = \frac{x_{\text{resp}}}{n_{\text{selected}}}, \quad p_{\text{max}} = \frac{x_{\text{resp}} + m}{n_{\text{selected}}}

First, the setup · once per SPSS session

Run this once each time you open SPSS, before any part. * Lecture connection: Target Population and Sampling Frame .
* Why: Validate and import the one provisional pickup roster before any dependent analysis .
* How: CD points to the folder containing the supplied CSV; GET DATA preserves the ID as text and imports numeric blanks as missing .
* How: The supplied validation rejects malformed nonblank numeric tokens and unexpected binary values before import .
* Read the result: H0 invitation frequencies account for the 2,400 recorded rows; that count does not certify frame completeness .
* Watch out: Running H1–H3 before H0 or pointing CD at the syntax file instead of its folder .
* Run: Choose File > Open > Syntax and open S05P_SPSS.sps; set CD to the extracted folder .
* Run: Select the complete CD-through-H0 block and choose Run > Selection .
* Run: Use Window to open Output Viewer; find H0 Import and Frame Check .
* S05P supplied reproducible syntax. Edit only the CD folder path; keep the CSV beside this file.
* Select and run the complete H0 block once per session before H1, H2 or H3.
CD 'REPLACE_WITH_FOLDER_CONTAINING_CSV_AND_SPS'.   * ← change only this path
BEGIN PROGRAM PYTHON3.
import csv
import math
import os
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
path = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'cedar_loop_pickups.csv')
expected = ['pickup_id', 'invitation_status', 'delay_flag', 'slow_flag', 'duration']
with open(path, newline='', encoding='utf-8-sig') as source:
    reader = csv.DictReader(source)
    if reader.fieldnames != expected:
        raise ValueError('H0 input error: CSV headers do not match the supplied data dictionary')
    rows = list(reader)
if len(rows) != 2400:
    raise ValueError('H0 input error: expected 2400 recorded pickup rows')
for line_number, row in enumerate(rows, start=2):
    if not row['pickup_id'] or row['invitation_status'] not in ('responded', 'nonresponse', 'not_invited'):
        raise ValueError('H0 input error: invalid identifier or invitation status on CSV line {}'.format(line_number))
    for field in ('delay_flag', 'slow_flag', 'duration'):
        token = row[field]
        if token == '':
            continue
        try:
            value = Decimal(token)
            if not value.is_finite() or not math.isfinite(float(value)):
                raise InvalidOperation
        except (InvalidOperation, ValueError, OverflowError):
            raise ValueError('H0 input error: malformed nonblank {} on CSV line {}'.format(field, line_number))
        if field in ('delay_flag', 'slow_flag') and value not in (Decimal(0), Decimal(1)):
            raise ValueError('H0 input error: {} must be 0, 1 or blank on CSV line {}'.format(field, line_number))
print('H0 CSV validation passed: 2400 rows; blank numeric tokens remain missing.')
END PROGRAM.
* Read the data file into SPSS (file type, name, and each variable's format).
GET DATA
 /TYPE=TXT
 /FILE='cedar_loop_pickups.csv'
 /ENCODING='UTF8'
 /DELCASE=LINE
 /DELIMITERS=","
 /QUALIFIER='"'
 /ARRANGEMENT=DELIMITED
 /FIRSTCASE=2
 /VARIABLES=pickup_id A8 invitation_status A16 delay_flag F1.0 slow_flag F1.0 duration F24.15.
* Attach readable descriptions to variables (they appear in output tables).
VARIABLE LABELS duration 'Recorded pickup duration (minutes)' delay_flag 'Delay over 50 minutes: 1 yes, 0 no' slow_flag 'Alias of delay_flag: 1 yes, 0 no'.
* Set each variable's measurement level (nominal, ordinal, scale).
VARIABLE LEVEL pickup_id (NOMINAL) invitation_status (NOMINAL) delay_flag (NOMINAL) slow_flag (NOMINAL) duration (SCALE).
* Run the pending transformations now.
EXECUTE.
* Name the output block so you can find it in the Viewer.
TITLE 'H0 Import and Frame Check'.
* Frequency table: how many cases fall in each category.
FREQUENCIES VARIABLES=invitation_status /ORDER=ANALYSIS.

Green lines start with *: they are comments that explain the command below them, and SPSS ignores them. Every command ends with a period.

* Lecture connection: Nonresponse Sensitivity Bounds .
* Why: Inspect invited statuses and observed delay outcomes that underpin Part A's denominators .
* How: FREQUENCIES lists exact invitation_status categories and recorded delay_flag values; blank flags remain missing .
* How: Do not equate all missing flags with invited nonresponse: most recorded rows were not invited .
* Read the result: Read status counts separately from the valid 0/1 delay count; Excel calculates the invitation scenarios .
* Watch out: Mistaking 2,300 missing delay flags for 2,300 invited nonrespondents .
* Run: In Syntax Editor, find H1 and select its complete titled block .
* Run: Choose Run > Selection; use Window to reach Output Viewer .
* Run: Find H1 Invitation and Recorded Delay Frequencies and inspect both tables .
TITLE 'H1 Invitation and Recorded Delay Frequencies'.
* Frequency table: how many cases fall in each category.
FREQUENCIES VARIABLES=invitation_status /ORDER=ANALYSIS.
* Make the next transformation apply to the next procedure only.
TEMPORARY.
* Keep only the rows that meet the condition (others are deleted).
SELECT IF (invitation_status = 'responded' AND (delay_flag = 0 OR delay_flag = 1)).
* Frequency table: how many cases fall in each category.
FREQUENCIES VARIABLES=delay_flag /ORDER=ANALYSIS.

sheet IN-CLASS_Lab Part B · answers email question 2

Part B · Duration Estimation and Confidence Intervals

⏱ 10 min
From slide 46 → work this card → Back to slide 47 · bring: The 95% CI bounds [39.62, 44.38] minutes and comparison to the 40-minute benchmark.

What the session covered · Section 2 Sampling Distributions, Standard Error, and Mean Estimation

  • Standard Error of the Mean: The standard error measures the expected variability of sample means across repeated samples of size n drawn from the same population. Dividing the standard deviation by sample size n instead of the square root of n.
  • Student t Confidence Interval for a Mean: A Student t confidence interval provides a range of plausible values for an unknown population mean when population spread is estimated by s. Claiming that 95 percent of individual customer pickup times fall within this narrow interval.

Slides 29–46

Full Toolkit

The rules you are applying

Standard Error of the Mean

SExˉ=sn \text{SE}_{\bar{x}} = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}

Student t Confidence Interval for a Mean

xˉ±t∗⋅sn,df=n−1 \bar{x} \pm t^* \cdot \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}, \quad \text{df} = n - 1

* Lecture connection: Student t Confidence Interval for a Mean .
* Why: Cross-check Part B's interval for average observed pickup duration .
* How: EXAMINE uses nonmissing duration in minutes; DESCRIPTIVES requests valid N, mean, sample SD, SE and 95% confidence limits .
* How: The interval estimates a mean, using sample spread rather than known population sigma .
* Read the result: Read H2 Descriptives' mean limits in minutes and compare with B10:B11 to displayed precision .
* Watch out: Confusing the mean interval with the range covering individual pickups .
* Run: After H0, find H2 in Syntax Editor and select its complete titled block .
* Run: Choose Run > Selection; switch through Window to Output Viewer .
* Run: Read H2 Mean Duration Interval, especially Descriptives and its mean limits .
TITLE 'H2 Mean Duration Interval'.
* Explore a variable: percentiles, spread and plots, optionally by group.

 /PLOT=NONE
 /STATISTICS=DESCRIPTIVES
 /CINTERVAL 95
 /MISSING=LISTWISE.

sheet IN-CLASS_Lab Part C · answers email question 3

Part C · Proportion Confidence Interval and Sample Size Planning

⏱ 10 min
From slide 66 → work this card → Back to slide 70 · bring: The 438-order sample size requirement and the decision guardrail memo recommendation.

What the session covered · Section 3 Proportion Estimation, Sample Size Planning, and Decision Guardrails

  • Confidence Interval for a Population Proportion: A proportion confidence interval bounds the true population share of binary events using the normal approximation. Reporting the margin of error in percentage terms without clarifying percentage points.
  • Sample Size Planning for Precision: Sample size planning calculates the minimum number of completed units needed to guarantee a specified margin of error at a given confidence level. Rounding down to the nearest whole integer instead of always rounding up to the next integer.
Course slides
Slides 48–66
Meaning of a Population Proportion and Point… 49 · One-Sample Confidence Interval for a Population… 51–53 · Constructing the Cedar Loop Confidence Interval 54 · What sample size planning means in business… 56 · Sample Size Formula for a Population Proportion 57–60 · Worked sample size calculation for Cedar Loop… 61
Concise Toolkit
pp. 18-26
Cedar Loop Grocery Pickup p. 20
Full Toolkit
pp. 44-61
Confidence Interval for a Population Proportion p. 48 · Cedar Loop Grocery Pickup p. 45

The rules you are applying

Confidence Interval for a Population Proportion

p^±z∗p^(1−p^)n \hat{p} \pm z^* \sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}(1 - \hat{p})}{n}}

Sample Size Planning for Precision

n=(z∗)2⋅p⋅(1−p)E2 n = \frac{(z^*)^2 \cdot p \cdot (1 - p)}{E^2}

import csv
import math
import os
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
path = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'cedar_loop_pickups.csv')
expected = ['pickup_id', 'invitation_status', 'delay_flag', 'slow_flag', 'duration']
with open(path, newline='', encoding='utf-8-sig') as source:
    reader = csv.DictReader(source)
    if reader.fieldnames != expected:
        raise ValueError('H0 input error: CSV headers do not match the supplied data dictionary')
    rows = list(reader)
if len(rows) != 2400:
    raise ValueError('H0 input error: expected 2400 recorded pickup rows')
for line_number, row in enumerate(rows, start=2):
    if not row['pickup_id'] or row['invitation_status'] not in ('responded', 'nonresponse', 'not_invited'):
        raise ValueError('H0 input error: invalid identifier or invitation status on CSV line {}'.format(line_number))
    for field in ('delay_flag', 'slow_flag', 'duration'):
        token = row[field]
        if token == '':
            continue
        try:
            value = Decimal(token)
            if not value.is_finite() or not math.isfinite(float(value)):
                raise InvalidOperation
        except (InvalidOperation, ValueError, OverflowError):
            raise ValueError('H0 input error: malformed nonblank {} on CSV line {}'.format(field, line_number))
        if field in ('delay_flag', 'slow_flag') and value not in (Decimal(0), Decimal(1)):
            raise ValueError('H0 input error: {} must be 0, 1 or blank on CSV line {}'.format(field, line_number))
print('H0 CSV validation passed: 2400 rows; blank numeric tokens remain missing.')
END PROGRAM.

What the session covered · Section 3 Proportion Estimation, Sample Size Planning, and Decision Guardrails

  • Confidence Interval for a Population Proportion: A proportion confidence interval bounds the true population share of binary events using the normal approximation. Reporting the margin of error in percentage terms without clarifying percentage points.
  • Sample Size Planning for Precision: Sample size planning calculates the minimum number of completed units needed to guarantee a specified margin of error at a given confidence level. Rounding down to the nearest whole integer instead of always rounding up to the next integer.

The rules you are applying

Confidence Interval for a Population Proportion

p^±z∗p^(1−p^)n \hat{p} \pm z^* \sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}(1 - \hat{p})}{n}}

Sample Size Planning for Precision

n=(z∗)2⋅p⋅(1−p)E2 n = \frac{(z^*)^2 \cdot p \cdot (1 - p)}{E^2}
